description: DEF CON 32 Creator Stage showcases technical presentations, hardware demonstrations, and research by independent security creators, builders, and practitioners. Talks cover embedded exploitation, automotive and avionics security, bug bounty tradecraft, operational technology, and practical community education.

talks.title: Your Smartcard Is Dumb: A Brief History of Hacking Access Control Systems
talks.teaser: Examines how physical access control systems and smartcard readers operate, detailing high-profile flaws and fundamental design vulnerabilities.
talks.summary:
Physical Access Control Architecture

Physical access control systems rely on card readers, controllers, and electronic locking mechanisms to secure physical spaces. When a credential card is tapped against a reader, specific identifying data is transmitted, processed, and evaluated to trigger door unlock mechanisms.

Mechanisms and Reader Interactions

Card readers interrogate RFID and smartcard credentials to extract badge IDs and access codes. The communication between the card, the reader interface, and the backend controller introduces distinct points of exposure across the physical infrastructure.

High Profile Access Control Exploits

Numerous high-profile vulnerabilities afflict widely deployed access control systems. Architectural weaknesses in legacy credential formatting and transmission protocols allow attackers to bypass door controllers and compromise physical entry points.

Design Flaws and Mitigation Strategies

Fundamental design assumptions in popular access systems frequently fail to provide adequate tamper resistance or cryptographic verification. Upgrading to modern authenticated credentials and supervised reader wiring mitigates common badge cloning and replay attacks.

talks.title: What to Expect When You’re Exploiting: 0Days, Baby Monitors & Wi-Fi Cams
talks.teaser: Uncovers zero-day vulnerabilities in cloud-connected Wi-Fi cameras and baby monitors, demonstrating remote code execution via flawed P2P protocols.
talks.summary:
Cloud Connected Camera Attack Surface

Consumer Wi-Fi cameras and baby monitors provide convenient remote video monitoring through mobile and cloud interfaces. However, the affordability of these IoT devices often correlates with flawed security implementations that expose end users to serious privacy risks.

Local Root and Management Platform Exploitation

Exploration of multiple camera models revealed methods to obtain local root access on target devices. Additionally, researchers identified a zero-day vulnerability in a widely used IoT device management platform that allows unauthorized remote access and control across millions of deployed cameras worldwide.

Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via P2P

Analysis of the underlying peer-to-peer (P2P) networking protocols demonstrated an inherently flawed implementation. Attackers can leverage these protocol flaws to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution and intercept live camera feeds without valid credentials.

Remediation and Secure Deployment

Securing home surveillance devices requires patching firmware flaws, restricting cloud management permissions, and isolating camera traffic on segmented local network VLANs.

talks.title: Using AI Computer Vision in Your OSINT Data Analysis
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how AI-driven computer vision on cloud platforms accelerates OSINT analysis through object detection, facial recognition, and chronolocation.
talks.summary:
Overcoming OSINT Data Volume Challenges

Open-source intelligence investigations routinely collect vast repositories of images and video recordings. Manually analyzing this voluminous visual data is time-consuming and risks overlooking subtle artifacts in foreground and background elements.

Cloud Based Computer Vision Pipelines

Leveraging computer vision services across AWS and Azure enables automated, high-speed analysis of large visual datasets. Cloud-based AI pipelines process forensic visual evidence using object detection, facial recognition, optical character recognition (OCR), and voice-to-text conversion.

Chronolocation and Evidence Correlation

Applying chronolocation analysis correlates timestamps, location markers, and identified visual artifacts to reconstruct real-world timelines. This approach assists investigators in establishing precise narratives, such as tracking individuals and objects across specific locations and times.

Operational Recommendations for Analysts

Integrating automated computer vision workflows significantly increases analytical throughput while maintaining investigative rigor. Implementing structured tagging and verification methods ensures accurate evidence correlation across complex multi-source investigations.

talks.title: Offensive Security Testing: Safeguarding the Final Frontier
talks.teaser: Details offensive security assessments of open-source space mission control systems NASA OpenMCT and YaMCS to uncover chained exploit paths.
talks.summary:
Evolution of Space Mission Control Systems

Mission Control Systems (MCS) serve as the primary ground interface for monitoring and commanding space assets. Modern architectures have shifted from isolated control rooms to networked and remotely accessible deployments, exposing mission software to conventional cyber threats.

Security Posture in Space Software Development

Despite adopting modern technology stacks, space software development frequently defers security considerations to late lifecycle stages. Established open-source mission control systems often harbor fundamental vulnerabilities that can jeopardize operational spacecraft.

Vulnerability Analysis in OpenMCT and YaMCS

Security evaluations of NASA OpenMCT and Yamcs identified multiple exploitable vulnerabilities. When chained together, these weaknesses enable unauthorized ground-segment access and compromise command pipelines regulating active space missions.

Integrating Offensive Security Testing

Proactively embedding offensive security testing into the space software development lifecycle is essential. Rigorous adversarial assessments identify architectural weaknesses before mission systems deploy into operational ground stations.

talks.title: XR for All: Accessibility and Privacy for Disabled Users
talks.teaser: Examines core privacy risks and accessibility hurdles faced by disabled users in extended reality platforms and highlights open-source solutions.
talks.summary:
Accessibility Hurdles in Extended Reality

Extended Reality (XR) platforms offer immersive environments for social interaction, training, and remote collaboration. However, many disabled users encounter systemic barriers that exclude them from fully participating in XR technologies.

Tensions Between Privacy and Assistive Tools

Assistive technologies in XR frequently require continuous tracking of user motion, eye gaze, and biometric responses. The extensive telemetry collected to enable accessibility often creates severe privacy risks if stored or shared without adequate protections.

Open Source Accessibility Initiatives

Efforts spearheaded by the XR Access Initiative at Cornell Tech focus on establishing open-source standards and tools that balance user accessibility with robust data protection and privacy guarantees.

talks.title: How State Laws Meant to Protect Children Raise Other Risks
talks.teaser: Explores how state youth privacy legislation creates unintended privacy risks by mandating sensitive personal data collection and impacts online speech.
talks.summary:
State Youth Privacy Legislative Trends

State legislatures across the United States have introduced and passed laws aimed at safeguarding minors on online platforms and social media networks. These statutory initiatives attempt to impose strict usage restrictions and data protections for younger audiences.

Unintended Data Collection Risks

To enforce age-based access controls, online services are required to verify the age and identity of users. This mandate forces platforms to collect extensive sensitive personal data and government identification from both minors and adults, exacerbating data breach risks.

First Amendment and Free Speech Concerns

Mandatory age verification mechanisms raise significant constitutional and First Amendment challenges. Legal disputes surrounding California's Age Appropriate Design Code Act highlight how restrictive verification requirements can chill protected speech and limit anonymous access to information.

Balancing Child Safety and User Privacy

Developing effective youth protection policies requires balancing safety objectives with privacy rights. Frameworks must focus on minimizing data collection while ensuring age-appropriate platform defaults.

talks.title: Winning the Game of Active Directory
talks.teaser: Walks through attack paths in the Game of Active Directory lab environment and demonstrates practical misconfiguration mitigations.
talks.summary:
The Game of Active Directory Environment

Game of Active Directory (GOAD) is a vulnerable lab environment designed for penetration testers to practice domain exploitation techniques. It contains over thirty distinct attack vectors demonstrating paths to full domain compromise.

Exploiting Common AD Misconfigurations

Penetration testers navigate complex Active Directory networks by chaining misconfigured permissions, weak credential handling, and default domain policies. Exploiting these flaws allows rapid lateral movement and domain privilege escalation.

Implementing Robust Mitigations

Securing Active Directory environments requires addressing underlying misconfigurations rather than relying solely on detection. Implementing credential hygiene, fine-grained access controls, and least-privilege delegation effectively neutralizes common attack chains.

Practical Hardening Strategies

Defenders validate security posture by verifying that deployed configuration changes successfully block known exploitation paths across domain controllers and joined workstations.

talks.title: Warflying in a Cessna
talks.teaser: Analyzes airborne Wi-Fi signal propagation and reconnaissance data collected by warflying a small Cessna aircraft at various altitudes.
talks.summary:
Concept and Motivation Behind Warflying

Combining airborne flight with traditional wireless wardriving techniques allows researchers to measure radio frequency leakage at altitude. Flying a Cessna equipped with wireless monitoring gear enables large-scale geographic signal mapping.

Hardware Setup and Flight Safety

Executing aerial reconnaissance requires careful preparation regarding aviation safety regulations, equipment power constraints, and antenna placement within a small general aviation aircraft.

Signal Capture at High Altitudes

Flight tests conducted at altitudes of 1500 to 2500 feet collected substantial wireless traffic from ground-based access points. Signal propagation data reveals how far terrestrial Wi-Fi signals escape into the atmosphere and are detectable from the air.

Data Processing and Analysis

Geospatial analysis of the captured wireless packets highlights the density of unencrypted and misconfigured access points visible from civilian aircraft altitudes.

talks.title: V2GEvil: Ghost in the Wires
talks.teaser: Introduces a specialized security testing tool targeting Electric Vehicle Communication Controllers and ISO 15118 on-board charging protocols.
talks.summary:
Electric Vehicle Charging Communication Security

Modern electric vehicles rely on Electric Vehicle Communication Controllers (EVCC) and On-Board Charging (OBC) systems to negotiate power transfer with charging stations. These communication channels form a critical interface between automotive systems and electrical grid infrastructure.

ISO 15118 Protocol Vulnerabilities

Investigating the ISO 15118 vehicle-to-grid (V2G) standard revealed architectural vulnerabilities in charging port interfaces and digital handshake protocols that can be exploited during charging sessions.

The V2GEvil Security Assessment Tool

Researchers developed the V2GEvil testing toolkit to probe and evaluate communication controllers in electric vehicles, identifying firmware flaws and protocol weaknesses that impact charging reliability.

Securing Grid and Vehicle Interfaces

Hardening vehicle-to-grid communications requires enforcing strict mutual authentication, cryptographic validation, and continuous monitoring of charging controllers against unauthorized manipulation.

talks.title: War Games: Red Team for OT Based on Real-World Case Studies
talks.teaser: Shares tactical insights and attack vectors from a decade of offensive red team simulations inside large-scale industrial control environments.
talks.summary:
Industrial Red Teaming Experience

Executing offensive attack simulations against operational technology (OT) and industrial control systems (ICS) requires specialized methodologies to evaluate cyber-physical resilience without disrupting physical operations.

TTPs and Attack Vectors in Industrial Networks

Analysis of red team engagements across global industrial facilities reveals common tactics, techniques, and procedures used to bridge corporate IT networks into isolated OT enclaves.

Network Propagation and Lifecycle Execution

Attackers leverage protocol weaknesses, legacy trust relationships, and unsegmented engineering workstations to establish command and control across the complete ICS-OT attack lifecycle.

Case Studies in Penetrating Cyber Physical Systems

Real-world case studies illustrate successful penetration of industrial operations, demonstrating how cyber intrusions can directly impact physical process controllers and safety systems.

talks.title: You Got a Lighter? I Need to Do Some Electroporation
talks.teaser: Examines historical biological warfare precedents, emerging threats at the intersection of AI and bioweaponry, and the need for defensive norms.
talks.summary:
Historical Precedents of Biological Warfare

Biological warfare has deep historical roots extending back to ancient conflicts. Reviewing historical implementations provides vital context for understanding how biological threats evolve and where modern defenses must focus.

Emerging AI Capabilities in Bioweaponry

Advances in artificial intelligence and generative modeling accelerate molecular discovery while lowering barriers to developing biological agents. The integration of AI into biotechnology poses critical challenges for national and international security.

Addressing Failures of Imagination

Technological vulnerabilities are frequently compounded by failures of imagination in threat modeling. Proactive defensive strategies must anticipate novel combination attacks that leverage interconnected technologies.

Cultivating Global Norms and Transparency

Safeguarding against the malevolent exploitation of biological agents requires establishing clear social norms, fostering international transparency, and building practical defensive countermeasures.

talks.title: The Past, Present, and Future of Bioweapons
talks.teaser: Explores historical precedents of biological warfare, generative AI risks in bioweapon proliferation, and strategies for global defense transparency.
talks.summary:
Evolution of Biological Threats

Biological warfare encompasses centuries of strategic development, from conventional historical dissemination methods to contemporary biotechnology applications. Understanding this historical arc is vital for designing effective biodefense architectures.

Impact of Generative AI on Proliferation

Generative AI models and automated laboratory pipelines present new risks by simplifying biological agent design. Panelists assess how technological democratization and information proliferation influence bioweapon development.

Countering Disinformation and Normalization

Online information environments and public desensitization to hostile cyber and biological incidents create challenges for establishing defensive consensus and identifying coordinated threat activities.

Building Resilient Defensive Frameworks

Mitigating biological threats requires fostering scientific transparency, establishing robust international governance standards, and developing multidisciplinary defensive surveillance systems.

talks.title: The Interplay Between Safety and Security in Aviation Systems
talks.teaser: Breaks down civil aviation certification frameworks including DO-356A and ARP4754B to show how safety analyses inform threat modeling and security assurance.
talks.summary:
Aviation Certification Foundations

Civil aviation safety has traditionally relied on established engineering standards such as DO-178. As aircraft architectures incorporate widespread digital connectivity, security standards like DO-356A have become essential components of modern airworthiness certification.

Safety Analyses and Design Assurance Levels

Development standards ARP4754B and ARP4761A define system development and safety analysis processes. Design Assurance Levels (DAL) quantify system criticality based on potential failure condition severity.

Bridging Safety Analyses into Threat Modeling

Safety hazard assessments directly inform security threat models. Analyzing architectural interdependencies enables engineers to identify where cyber threats could trigger critical safety failures across airborne equipment.

Security Assurance Levels and Mitigations

Security mitigations are assigned specific Security Assurance Levels (SAL). Implementing verified security controls ensures that software and hardware components meet airworthiness compliance mandates.

talks.title: RF Attacks on Aviation's Defense Against Mid-Air Collisions
talks.teaser: Demonstrates practical RF attacks against TCAS II collision avoidance systems to forge resolution advisories and disable collision detection.
talks.summary:
Aviation Collision Avoidance Architecture

The Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS II) serves as an onboard safety net preventing mid-air collisions. Historically, TCAS attacks remained theoretical due to timing constraints and implicit receiver properties.

Practical RF Exploitation with COTS Hardware

Researchers built practical radio frequency attack tooling using commercial off-the-shelf software-defined radios. The tooling successfully injects crafted transponder signals to manipulate cockpit collision avoidance displays.

Forging Traffic and Resolution Advisories

Crafted RF transmissions generate phantom aircraft and force TCAS to trigger false Traffic Advisories (TA) and Resolution Advisories (RA), commanding pilots to execute unnecessary evasive maneuvers.

Disabling TCAS Collision Capabilities

A secondary attack mechanism remotely suppresses an aircraft's TCAS processing, blinding collision detection systems and highlighting urgent vulnerabilities in legacy avionics protocols.

talks.title: Physical OSINT
talks.teaser: Introduces foundational open-source intelligence methods and resources for gathering facility and site intelligence prior to physical visits.
talks.summary:
Foundations of Physical OSINT

Open-source intelligence principles apply directly to physical security assessments and facility investigations. Publicly accessible information provides extensive insight into physical infrastructure, access controls, and site layouts.

Scoping and Initial Investigation Steps

Starting a physical investigation begins with identifying public records, business filings, satellite imagery, and social media footprints related to a target location and its operational staff.

Expert Tools and Data Sources

Investigators utilize specialized mapping databases, architectural registries, permit filings, and metadata extraction tools to map facility perimeters, camera placements, and badge reader types before arriving on site.

Operational Preparation for Physical Assessments

Synthesizing open-source data into an actionable intelligence brief optimizes on-site red team reconnaissance and minimizes operational footprint during physical penetration tests.

talks.title: Curious Case of Alice & Bob: What You Can Do as Digital Investigators
talks.teaser: Walks through a real-world investigative narrative to show how digital artifacts in system registries fit into broader forensic investigations.
talks.summary:
Narrative Driven Digital Investigation

Digital forensics investigations require moving beyond raw technical indicators to understand how individual clues fit into a broader case narrative. Framing investigative workflows around structured scenarios clarifies evidentiary relationships.

Uncovering Windows Registry Artifacts

System registries, event logs, and user activity artifacts contain critical forensic evidence. Locating and interpreting these keys reveals execution history, connected devices, and file interactions.

Contextualizing Evidence in Case Work

Determining why specific digital artifacts exist and how they correlate with timeline events allows investigators to reconstruct attacker actions or insider activity accurately.

Realistic Expectations for Forensic Analysis

Balancing technical tool capabilities against evidentiary limitations establishes realistic benchmarks for what digital forensics can conclusively prove during incident response.

talks.title: So You Wanna Know How to Make Badges
talks.teaser: Guides makers through the complete electronic badge creation workflow from initial concept and PCB design to large-scale production.
talks.summary:
DEF CON Conference Presentation

This segment features remarks and presentations from DEF CON organizers and security leaders. Topics include the state of cybersecurity, hacker culture, community initiatives, and the conference's impact on the security landscape.

talks.title: Psychic Paper: Making E-Ink Access Badges Accessible for Anyone
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how smartphone apps can easily reprogram unprotected e-ink RFID badges to alter both the visual display and embedded credentials.
talks.summary:
E-Ink Access Badge Architecture

Modern electronic access badges incorporating e-ink displays allow users to update printed credentials digitally. These badges combine low-power e-ink screens with integrated RFID chips for physical access authentication.

Smartphone Reprogramming Vulnerabilities

Vendors supply smartphone applications to update the e-ink graphic display and configure badge credentials. However, many commercial e-ink badges implement zero cryptographic authentication or access restrictions.

Cloning and Credential Modification

Using publicly available smartphone applications, an attacker can overwrite the display graphics and reprogram RFID payload data, effectively transforming the badge into arbitrary credentials for unauthorized facility access.

Security Considerations for Visual and RFID Badges

Deploying smart access badges securely requires enforcing mutual authentication and cryptographic signing on all wireless programming interfaces to prevent unauthorized visual and digital tampering.

talks.title: Preparing for the Future: A Discussion of Our Rapidly Evolving Threat Landscape
talks.teaser: Panelists discuss how AI advances, deepfakes, global conflicts, and personal CISO liability are rapidly reshaping modern cybersecurity threats.
talks.summary:
The Shifting Global Threat Landscape

Over the past two years, global conflicts, macroeconomic pressures, and rapid technological breakthroughs have fundamentally altered cybersecurity operations across enterprise and government sectors.

AI Driven Attack Vectors and Deepfakes

Adversaries increasingly leverage automated tools and generative AI to rapidly generate exploits and create convincing audio-visual deepfakes. These capabilities enable sophisticated social engineering schemes that deceive experienced staff.

Regulatory Pressures and Executive Liability

Government regulations and corporate accountability standards now place direct personal liability on CISOs and security leadership during major breach disclosures, reshaping corporate governance priorities.

Strategic Adaptation for Defenders

Organizations must modernize threat intelligence pipelines, establish strict identity verification safeguards against synthetic media, and foster agile defense cultures to counter emerging threat actors.

talks.title: Student Engagement Doesn't Have to Suck
talks.teaser: Explores immersive metaverse environments and gamified teaching methods to improve student engagement in cybersecurity education.
talks.summary:
This DEF CON talk covers student engagement doesn't have to suck.

talks.title: Reverse Engineering and Hacking Ecovacs Robots
talks.teaser: Reveals critical security flaws in Ecovacs smart home robots including broken crypto, missing TLS validation, remote code execution, and camera eavesdropping.
talks.summary:
Smart Home Robot Security Posture

Modern robotic vacuums and air purifiers integrate high-definition cameras, microphone arrays, and continuous cloud connectivity. The security architecture of Ecovacs, a market leader in home robotics, was evaluated across multiple product lines.

Discovered Vulnerabilities and Attack Paths

Reverse engineering Ecovacs firmware and communication stacks uncovered widespread vulnerabilities, including broken cryptographic routines, absent TLS certificate validation, honor-system access controls, and multiple remote code execution (RCE) flaws.

Unauthorized Surveillance and Privacy Breaches

Exploiting identified firmware weaknesses allows unauthorized attackers to access live camera feeds, intercept audio recordings, and bypass factory reset protections without user consent.

Vendor Disclosure and Certification Failures

Researchers share challenges encountered during the vulnerability disclosure process and discuss why third-party security certifications frequently fail to ensure real-world IoT device security.

talks.title: Reflections on a Decade in Bug Bounties
talks.teaser: Shares insights from ten years of bug bounty hunting, focusing on bug chaining strategies and collaboration between hunters and triage teams.
talks.summary:
Ten Year Bug Bounty Journey

Transitioning from an entry-level researcher submitting low-impact findings to a seasoned bug hunter requires continuous learning, embracing duplicate reports, and refining testing methodologies over time.

Chaining Low Severity Findings for High Impact

High-value vulnerability research relies on chaining seemingly minor informational or low-severity flaws into critical application exploits that demonstrate tangible business risk.

Understanding the Triage Perspective

A triage specialist from Synack explains the criteria triage analysts use to evaluate bug submissions, clarifying the distinction between researcher viewpoints and client risk assessments.

Actionable Advice for Aspiring Hunters

Developing strong communication skills, submitting clear reproduction steps, and collaborating constructively with triage teams improves report acceptance rates and builds sustainable bounty careers.

talks.title: Programming a CTS-V Gauge Cluster into an ATS-V, Out of Pure Spite
talks.teaser: Details how to reverse engineer General Motors electronic gauge cluster programming to retrofit digital dashboards into unsupported vehicles.
talks.summary:
Automotive Electronics Retrofitting

Integrating digital gauge clusters from high-end vehicle models into unsupported platforms often encounters commercial gatekeeping and expensive proprietary reprogramming tools.

Reverse Engineering GM Firmware Protocols

Analyzing General Motors electronic control modules and CAN bus communications uncovered the specific firmware configuration parameters governing instrument cluster operation.

Overcoming Reprogramming Barriers

Developing custom software tools enabled direct flashing and calibration of the Cadillac CTS-V digital cluster to operate seamlessly within an ATS-V vehicle architecture.

Open Source Release and Documentation

Documenting the complete reverse engineering process and releasing reprogramming code openly on GitHub democratizes automotive hardware customization.

talks.title: Practical Exploitation of DoS in Bug Bounty
talks.teaser: Examines techniques for discovering high-impact Denial of Service flaws in bug bounties through N+1 database queries, GraphQL abuse, and cache poisoning.
talks.summary:
Denial of Service in Bounty Programs

Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerabilities disrupt application availability by exhausting server resources or exploiting architectural flaws. While often overlooked, demonstrating reproducible application DoS can yield significant bounty rewards.

N+1 Queries and Database Exhaustion

Applications that generate redundant database queries for individual user requests are vulnerable to N+1 query amplification attacks. Crafting requests that trigger thousands of unnecessary queries causes severe database latency and application crashes.

GraphQL Query Complexity and Cache Poisoning

Unconstrained GraphQL endpoints can be forced to resolve deeply nested or circular queries that consume excessive CPU and memory resources. Furthermore, web cache poisoning manipulates cached responses to serve errors or denial-of-service states to all subsequent users.

Responsible Testing and Reporting

Assessing DoS vulnerabilities requires careful testing to avoid impacting production availability. Reports must clearly demonstrate mathematical resource consumption without causing operational outages.

talks.title: Porn & Privacy
talks.teaser: Covers legal and practical strategies to defend against nonconsensual intimate image distribution, sextortion, and online stalking.
talks.summary:
Intersection of Digital Lives and Intimate Content

As social interactions increasingly occur across online platforms, individuals create and share sensitive personal content that requires rigorous privacy and security safeguards.

Legal Frameworks Surrounding Nonconsensual Distribution

Reviewing obscenity laws, statutory protections against nonconsensual distribution of intimate images (NCII), and legal classifications of sextortion provides essential context for victim recourse.

Preventing Information Leaks and Catfishing

Implementing strong account security, metadata scrubbing, and selective sharing habits helps prevent intimate material from being compromised by malicious actors or catfishing schemes.

Incident Response and Recovery Strategies

Victims of sextortion and image leaks require actionable recovery plans, including automated takedown requests, evidence preservation, and engagement with legal and advocacy resources.

talks.title: Open Source Hacker vs. Government Lawyer
talks.teaser: A former DoD attorney and an open-source engineer debate government cybersecurity inefficiencies and propose agile open-source solutions.
talks.summary:
The Cultural Divide in Defense Cybersecurity

A former Department of Defense attorney and an open-source software engineer debate the bureaucratic and technical bottlenecks hindering federal cybersecurity initiatives.

Decoding Government Policy Rationales

Complex defense procurement rules, compliance frameworks, and legacy mandates dictate government IT decisions, frequently resulting in sluggish hardware deployments and outdated security controls.

Private Sector Perspectives on Military Grade Tech

Critiquing the realities behind 'military-grade technology' highlights how rigid procurement processes often lag behind dynamic commercial and open-source software development practices.

Open Source Solutions for National Defense

Integrating open-source development workflows and modern vulnerability disclosure models can streamline DoD software supply chains while maintaining necessary security assurances.

talks.title: Detecting Persistent Threats on DrayTek Devices
talks.teaser: Reverse engineers DrayTek router firmware to uncover dynamic module persistence mechanisms and presents an open-source memory integrity detection tool.
talks.summary:
Targeting Edge Security Appliances

Threat actors increasingly compromise network perimeter devices such as VPN concentrators, routers, and firewalls. Many edge devices run proprietary, closed-source firmware that lacks visibility and integrity verification mechanisms.

Reverse Engineering DrayTek Firmware

Analyzing proprietary firmware across hundreds of thousands of Internet-exposed DrayTek routers revealed that the underlying RTOS kernel supports dynamic module loading. Uploaded code modules persist across reboots and firmware upgrades.

Developing Malicious Modules for Persistence

Researchers demonstrated how chaining newly discovered vulnerabilities with custom kernel modules establishes stealthy, durable persistence within edge routing infrastructure.

Memory Integrity Verification and Tooling

To counter persistent edge compromises, researchers built and released an open-source inspection module that validates loaded RTOS memory modules, restoring visibility for defenders.

talks.title: Sneaky Extensions: The MV3 Escape Artists
talks.teaser: Demonstrates stealthy data exfiltration and arbitrary code execution attacks bypassing Chrome Manifest V3 security restrictions.
talks.summary:
Browser Extensions in Modern Workspaces

Browser extensions have become essential workplace tools for video conferencing, collaboration, and productivity. However, extensions holding standard low-privilege permissions often expose end users to extensive privacy and security threats.

Security Boundaries in Manifest V3

Google introduced Manifest V3 (MV3) to restrict extension capabilities, notably banning dynamic script evaluation functions such as eval and new Function to prevent arbitrary code execution.

Bypassing Restrictions with Minimal Permissions

Researchers demonstrated attack techniques requiring only default permissions common to ninety-five percent of Chrome Web Store extensions. These methods execute arbitrary code and stealthily capture clipboard contents, webcam streams, and microphone feeds.

Cross Extension Credential Theft

Malicious extensions can abuse shared browser APIs to interfere with neighboring extensions, intercepting one-time passwords (OTPs), credit card details, and stored credentials from password managers.

talks.title: SBOMs the Hard Way: Hacking Bob the Minion
talks.teaser: Demonstrates hardware disassembly, SPI flash extraction, and JTAG interfacing to build an accurate Software Bill of Materials for an IoT Wi-Fi router.
talks.summary:
Challenges in Generating Hardware SBOMs

Generating an accurate Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for consumer IoT equipment typically requires access to vendor firmware packages. When manufacturers withhold firmware releases, conventional software analysis tools cannot be applied.

Hardware Disassembly and Chip Identification

Analyzing the Davolink 'Bob the Minion' Wi-Fi router began with complete physical disassembly, component inspection, and pinout identification across circuit boards.

SPI Flash Extraction and JTAG Debugging

Physical extraction techniques, including desoldering SPI flash memory and tapping JTAG/SWD debug interfaces, enabled direct binary dumps of the device's running firmware.

Constructing the SBOM and Reporting Vulnerabilities

Decompiling and inspecting the extracted firmware binaries produced a comprehensive software inventory, revealing unpatched component vulnerabilities that were reported to the vendor.

talks.title: Pick Your Poison: Navigating a Secure Clean Energy Transition
talks.teaser: Analyzes supply chain and cybersecurity policy challenges when integrating foreign-sourced components into clean energy infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Cybersecurity in Clean Energy Systems

The global transition to renewable power incorporates digitalized control systems across wind farms, solar arrays, and regional power utilities. However, many components are manufactured in foreign supply chains, introducing significant supply chain risks.

Limits of Rip and Replace Policies

Traditional 'rip and replace' mandates are economically and technically impractical when applied to widespread distributed energy infrastructure, requiring more nuanced risk management frameworks.

Operational and Physical Grid Realities

Securing clean energy networks demands an understanding of electrical grid physical dynamics, communication latency constraints, and operational realities governing municipal utilities.

Policy Frameworks for Energy Resilience

Balancing immediate climate deployment targets against long-term national security requires agile policy approaches that support continuous monitoring and resilient engineering controls.

talks.title: Safecracking for Everyone
talks.teaser: Introduces the mechanical principles, operational vulnerabilities, and manipulation techniques used in combination safecracking.
talks.summary:
Mechanical Safe Lock Architecture

Mechanical combination safes rely on wheel packs, drive cams, and fence mechanisms to secure locking bolts. Understanding how these mechanical components interact is fundamental to evaluating safe security.

Vulnerabilities in Wheel Pack Designs

Manufacturing tolerances, mechanical friction, and contact point dynamics introduce physical feedback cues into combination dial rotations.

Principles of Safe Manipulation

Safecracking via manipulation relies on systematically measuring wheel gate signatures and contact points, determining combination numbers non-destructively without drilling or damaging the safe.

Locksport and Physical Security Insights

Mastering safe manipulation provides security practitioners with practical insights into mechanical bypass techniques and the defensive design requirements for high-security containers.

talks.title: Small Satellite Modeling and Defender Software
talks.teaser: Shares findings from physical small satellite modeling, attack simulations, and the development of the lightweight Small Satellite Defender mitigation tool.
talks.summary:
Growth of Small Satellite Architectures

Commercial rideshare rocket launches have lowered the cost of deploying small satellite systems and CubeSats for academic, civil, and defense research missions.

Building a High Fidelity Satellite Testbed

Researchers developed realistic small satellite testbeds using embedded hardware, sensor arrays, radio transceivers, and orbital simulation engines to evaluate aerospace cybersecurity posture.

Simulating Space Attack Scenarios

Executing adversarial simulations against the testbed evaluated the impact of man-in-the-middle (MitM) command injection, denial-of-service, radio spoofing, and hardware fault injection.

The Small Satellite Defender Tool

To safeguard orbital platforms, researchers engineered 'Small Satellite Defender' (SSD), a lightweight onboard monitoring utility that validates incoming commands and enforces health telemetry checks.

talks.title: Signature-Based Detection Using Network Timing
talks.teaser: Explores building detection signatures from network transaction timing intervals to identify malicious command-and-control communication.
talks.summary:
Limitations of Static Network Signatures

Defenders traditionally identify malicious network traffic using byte patterns, domains, and IP reputations. However, payload encryption and dynamic infrastructure frequently render static signatures ineffective.

Timing Signatures in Packet Streams

Malware command-and-control channels exhibit distinct temporal patterns between network transactions. Measuring inter-packet timing intervals provides a robust telemetry dimension for behavioral fingerprinting.

Data Science and Python Packet Processing

Applying statistical analysis and Python packet processing pipelines to PCAP captures identifies timing signatures corresponding to known malware families and beaconing activity.

Practical Deployment in Threat Hunting

Integrating timing-based detection signatures into network monitoring tools enables security teams to detect encrypted command-and-control channels without inspecting payload content.

talks.title: RFID 101
talks.teaser: Explains RFID badge and reader communications, demonstrating cloning and brute-force techniques using Proxmark, Flipper Zero, and Keysy.
talks.summary:
Principles of RFID Access Systems

Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) systems operate across low-frequency (125 kHz) and high-frequency (13.56 MHz) bands to exchange identification tokens between access badges and fixed wall readers.

Reader and Badge Communication Dynamics

Interrogator coils energize passive RFID transponders via electromagnetic induction, prompting the transponder to transmit its encoded facility code and credential ID.

Tooling for Badge Cloning and Emulation

Security researchers utilize hardware tools including Proxmark3, Flipper Zero, and Keysy to sniff transmissions, clone legacy access cards, and emulate credentials in real time.

Brute Force Attacks and Access Mitigations

Unencrypted legacy formats allow attackers to brute-force valid badge numbers against readers. Transitioning to cryptographically signed credentials and mutual authentication prevents unauthorized badge duplication.

talks.title: Bypass 101
talks.teaser: Demonstrates physical entry bypass methods that defeat secured doors using egress and access control hardware flaws without picking locks.
talks.summary:
In this practical session on the DEF CON 32 Creator Stage, a physical penetration testing specialist presents "Bypass 101," a beginner-friendly overview of physical security vulnerabilities in commercial buildings and access control systems. At 03:00, the speaker demonstrates how common physical security mechanisms—such as crash bars and latch assemblies—can be bypassed in seconds using simple bypass tools without picking locks.

talks.title: Breaking Boundaries: Popping Shells in the Airgap with $10 & Arduino Magic
talks.teaser: Shows how to build an inexpensive wireless BadUSB device with Arduino hardware to execute payloads on airgapped medical systems.
talks.summary:
Airgapped Device Security Assumptions

Medical devices and laboratory systems are frequently isolated from corporate networks under the assumption that airgapping prevents cyber exploitation.

Wireless BadUSB Hardware Design

Using low-cost microcontroller boards and basic Arduino programming, researchers built a custom wireless BadUSB device for under ten dollars.

Executing Payloads on Isolated Systems

Connecting the device to an accessible USB port enables wireless command transmission, simulating keyboard keystrokes to execute local payloads and pop shells on non-networked systems.

Hardening Physical USB Interfaces

Protecting airgapped healthcare and industrial equipment requires disabling unused USB ports, enforcing physical port locks, and implementing strict peripheral access control policies.

talks.title: Exposing the Occultations in Large Off-Grid Solar Systems
talks.teaser: Reveals critical vulnerabilities in solar inverter management platforms that could allow attackers to manipulate power grid infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Solar Energy Management Architecture

Utility-scale and off-grid solar installations depend on cloud-managed smart inverters to monitor power output and regulate grid feed-in parameters.

Critical Vulnerabilities in Management Platforms

Security audits of prominent solar equipment manufacturers uncovered three critical vulnerabilities within cloud management portals and local inverter controller firmware.

Weaponization and Grid Stability Risks

Exploiting these flaws allows unauthorized remote attackers to alter power generation parameters, disconnect solar arrays simultaneously, and destabilize regional electrical grids.

National Security Implications and Defenses

Securing renewable energy infrastructure requires standardizing firmware verification protocols, isolating inverter management networks, and establishing rigorous vendor security oversight.

talks.title: Analyzing the Security of Satellite-Based Air Traffic Control
talks.teaser: Presents an in-depth security analysis of the satellite ADS-C aviation protocol, demonstrating message injection and position tampering using SDRs.
talks.summary:
Role of ADS-C in Oceanic Air Traffic

Automatic Dependent Surveillance–Contract (ADS-C) is a satellite datalink protocol utilized by air traffic control to monitor aircraft operating over oceanic and remote regions where terrestrial radar is unavailable.

Capturing and Decoding Satellite Telemetry

Using custom software-defined radio (SDR) receivers, researchers captured and decoded over 120,000 real-world ADS-C satellite messages, evaluating protocol structure and security properties.

Transmitter Implementation and Injection Attacks

Because ADS-C lacks cryptographic authentication, researchers constructed an SDR-based transmitter capable of crafting arbitrary uplink and downlink messages, altering reported aircraft positions, and forging flight contracts.

Assessment of Mitigations for Satellite Avionics

Evaluating potential countermeasures highlights the urgent need to introduce message authentication and encryption standards across satellite-based air traffic management networks.

talks.title: A Dive into the World of Aircraft PKI
talks.teaser: Details how public key infrastructure secures aircraft software parts and ground networks, addressing post-quantum transition challenges.
talks.summary:
Public Key Infrastructure in Commercial Aviation

Modern aircraft rely on Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) to establish trusted communications between onboard avionics, ground networks, and maintenance systems.

Securing Airborne Software Parts

Cryptographic signatures guarantee the authenticity and integrity of Field Loadable Software and electronic flight bag applications before installation on aircraft computers.

Aviation Regulations and Compliance Standards

International aviation authorities mandate strict certificate management policies and cryptographic validation procedures across the aircraft maintenance lifecycle.

Post Quantum Migration Considerations

The emergence of quantum computing poses significant risks to long-lifecycle embedded avionics systems, necessitating early adoption of post-quantum cryptographic algorithms in aerospace standards.

talks.title: UDSonCAN Attacks: Discovering Safety Critical Risks by Fuzzing
talks.teaser: Uncovers safety-critical vehicle vulnerabilities via UDSonCAN diagnostic fuzzing, demonstrating unauthenticated vehicle acceleration and braking.
talks.summary:
Diagnostic Services and Vehicle Safety

Unified Diagnostic Services over Controller Area Network (UDSonCAN) enables diagnostic communication with electronic control units (ECUs). Safety-critical diagnostic functions must be strictly gated by authentication when vehicles are in motion.

Fuzzing UDSonCAN Implementations

Systematic protocol fuzzing across production electric vehicle ECUs revealed diagnostic endpoints that execute without required SecurityAccess authentication checks.

Triggering Sudden Acceleration and Braking

Researchers demonstrated that injecting simple, unauthenticated diagnostic CAN frames can cause moving vehicles to brake abruptly or stationary vehicles to accelerate unexpectedly.

Automotive Countermeasures and ECU Hardening

Preventing unauthorized diagnostic execution requires enforcing robust cryptographic authentication, validating vehicle speed conditions in ECU firmware, and deploying CAN bus anomaly detection systems.

talks.title: The Village Peoples' Panel: What Really Goes On in a Village
talks.teaser: DEF CON village organizers share behind-the-scenes insights on funding, logistics, hardware setup, and managing volunteer teams.
talks.summary:
The Core Role of DEF CON Villages

Villages serve as hands-on learning environments and cultural hubs within the DEF CON ecosystem, providing specialized domains ranging from hardware hacking to lockpicking.

Logistics, Funding, and Equipment

Village staff discuss the logistical complexities of organizing a village, including securing corporate sponsorships, transporting heavy lab equipment, and managing network infrastructure.

Volunteer Coordination and Event Operations

Managing volunteer shifts, speaker schedules, and high attendee volumes requires proactive communication and mental health awareness to prevent burnout during intense multi-day conferences.

Lessons for Aspiring Community Builders

Experienced organizers share practical advice for starting new villages, fostering inclusive communities, and delivering engaging hands-on technical content.

talks.title: Bluetooth Blues: Unmasking CVE-2023-52709—The TI BLE5-Stack Attack
talks.teaser: Details the discovery and exploitation of CVE-2023-52709 in the Texas Instruments BLE5-Stack, causing denial of service in bonded peer devices.
talks.summary:
Bluetooth Low Energy Privacy Mechanisms

Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) utilizes Resolvable Private Addresses (RPAs) to prevent device tracking while maintaining authenticated bonding between trusted peers.

Discovery and Root Cause of CVE-2023-52709

Analysis of the Texas Instruments BLE5-Stack revealed a flaw where the stack fails to generate a valid Resolvable Private Address under specific connection sequences.

Denial of Service Against Bonded Peers

Exploiting this vulnerability creates a permanent Denial of Service (DoS) condition, preventing previously paired automotive and IoT peer devices from reconnecting.

Automotive Implications and Patch Deployment

Because TI BLE chipsets are widely integrated into automotive keyless entry systems and telematics units, deploying firmware patches is critical to restore reliable wireless pairing.

talks.title: The Wild and Wonderful World of Early Microprocessors with a Focus on 6502
talks.teaser: Explores the architecture and assembly programming of vintage 8-bit microprocessors, focusing on the MOS 6502 and retrocomputing platforms.
talks.summary:
The Dawn of Microprocessor Computing

In the 1970s and 1980s, early microprocessors such as the Z80, MOS 6502, 6809, and 68000 launched the personal computing revolution, powering iconic systems like the Apple II, Commodore 64, and Atari 8-bit computers.

MOS 6502 Architectural Fundamentals

The MOS 6502 stood out for its low production cost, streamlined instruction set, and efficient zero-page addressing modes, making it a favorite for hobbyists and embedded engineers.

Programming in 8-Bit Assembly

Writing assembly code directly for the 6502 reveals foundational hardware interactions, memory management constraints, and hardware register manipulation that remain relevant to modern embedded systems.

Modern Retrocomputing and Hardware Building

Hacker communities continue to build new custom hardware, develop modern software, and reverse engineer classic architectures using vintage 6502 microprocessor designs.

talks.title: Building a Secure Resilient Nationwide EV Charging Network
talks.teaser: Provides a White House policy perspective on systemic cybersecurity risks in national electric vehicle charging networks and grid integration.
talks.summary:
National Electrification and Grid Security

Federal investments in nationwide electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure connect thousands of public chargers to power grids, payment networks, and cloud management backends.

Systemic Cyber Risks in EV Ecosystems

Connecting millions of high-power charging units introduces systemic vulnerabilities where coordinated cyber attacks on EV chargers could trigger severe electrical grid disturbances.

Federal Policy Initiatives and Standards

Policymakers across federal agencies are establishing cybersecurity baselines, vulnerability testing protocols, and hardware resilience standards for federally funded charging stations.

Engaging the Hacker Community

Collaborating with independent security researchers and white-hat hackers is vital to discovering zero-day vulnerabilities in charging protocols before adversaries can exploit them.

talks.title: Behind the Badge: How We Used Hardware to Make AV Badge
talks.teaser: Walks through the hardware engineering behind an Aerospace Village badge featuring an integrated low-cost Linux system and ADS-B receiver.
talks.summary:
Reinventing Aerospace Conference Badges

ADS-B flight tracking traditionally requires a Raspberry Pi paired with dedicated USB software-defined radio receivers. The Aerospace Village badge project set out to design an autonomous, low-cost handheld receiver badge.

Low Cost Linux Hardware Architecture

Engineers integrated an entire system-on-chip running embedded Linux, selecting components that cost less than standard high-end microcontrollers while providing robust processing capability.

Custom Signal Processing Chain

A custom RF front end and demodulation processing pipeline was developed to capture and decode 1090 MHz ADS-B aircraft broadcast signals directly on the badge.

Onboard Mapping and Visualizations

The badge renders real-time aircraft positions and flight telemetry on an onboard display, demonstrating sophisticated embedded RF engineering on an event badge budget.

talks.title: Anyone Can Hack IoT: Beginner’s Guide to Hacking Your First IoT Device
talks.teaser: Provides a beginner-friendly methodology and budget hardware toolkit guide for disassembling, extracting firmware, and hacking IoT devices.
talks.summary:
Demystifying IoT Security Research

Hardware hacking is frequently perceived as prohibitively difficult and requiring expensive laboratory equipment. A structured, practical methodology allows anyone with basic technical skills to assess IoT devices.

Building a Sub-$100 Hardware Toolkit

Assembling an effective starter toolkit requires only inexpensive essentials, including a multimeter, USB-to-UART bridge, logic analyzer, and basic soldering tools.

Target Selection and Firmware Extraction

Choosing accessible consumer devices simplifies initial learning. Techniques for opening enclosures, locating UART serial pins, and dumping SPI flash memory reveal device operating systems.

Identifying Initial Footholds and Vulnerabilities

Analyzing extracted root filesystems allows beginners to uncover hardcoded credentials, unauthenticated debug shells, and vulnerable web management services.

talks.title: Access Control Done Right the First Time
talks.teaser: Shares engineering best practices for deploying robust physical access control systems, from encrypted reader wiring to badge management.
talks.summary:
Pitfalls of Minimum Viable Installations

Commercial access control installations often implement minimum viable configurations that leave physical entry points vulnerable to simple bypasses and wire tampering.

Supervised Wiring and Encryption Standards

Securing reader-to-controller communications requires implementing end-to-end encryption protocols like OSDP and supervised line resistors to detect wire tapping and tampering.

Selecting Clone Resistant Credentials

Organizations must replace legacy unencrypted 125 kHz RFID cards with modern, cryptographically authenticated high-frequency smartcards and properly configured reader keys.

Controller Hardening and Lifecycle Maintenance

Securing central controller enclosures, maintaining updated badge assignment databases, and performing regular physical audits ensures long-term facility security.

talks.title: 3DU: Homo ex Machina
talks.teaser: Examines FDA regulatory challenges and security requirements surrounding point-of-care 3D-printed medical device production systems.
talks.summary:
Point of Care 3D Medical Device Production

Personalized healthcare increasingly utilizes 3D printing directly at the hospital point of care (POC). The FDA's framework on Medical Device Production Systems (MDPS) categorizes in-hospital printing systems as regulated medical devices.

Stakeholder Dynamics in Hospital Deployments

Deploying on-site medical manufacturing requires close collaboration between healthcare delivery organizations (HDOs), device manufacturers (MDMs), and regulatory agencies.

Integrating AI into Production Systems

Artificial intelligence models optimize print parameters, material tolerances, and structural integrity for patient-specific implants and surgical guides.

Cybersecurity and Quality Assurance Challenges

Safeguarding point-of-care medical manufacturing demands secure design pipelines, validated CAD file integrity, and stringent quality control protocols to protect patient safety.

talks.title: Attacks on GenAI Data & Using Vector Encryption to Stop Them
talks.teaser: Explains embedding inversion attacks against generative AI vector databases and introduces open-source vector encryption for private search.
talks.summary:
Security Gaps in Vector Databases

The rapid adoption of generative AI tools has led to massive stores of sensitive health, financial, and HR data being indexed inside vector databases without native encryption controls.

Embedding Inversion Attacks

Contrary to common assumptions, vector embeddings are not secure one-way hashes. Inversion attacks can reconstruct original text, faces, and documents directly from stored vector embeddings.

Vector Encryption Cryptographic Principles

Researchers developed vector encryption algorithms that enable privacy-preserving similarity searches over fully encrypted vectors without decrypting underlying embeddings.

Open Source Implementation and Tradeoffs

Benchmarking open-source vector encryption tooling demonstrates practical trade-offs between computational latency, search accuracy, and mathematical data privacy.

talks.title: Simulating Attacks Against Hydroelectric Power Plants
talks.teaser: Demonstrates full-chain adversary emulation against a hydroelectric power plant firing range and details the resulting incident response analysis.
talks.summary:
Value of ICS Firing Ranges

Evaluating critical infrastructure cybersecurity requires realistic simulation environments. An ICS firing range was constructed to model the physical processes and network architecture of a hydroelectric power station.

Firing Range Architecture and Flooding Scenario

The testbed simulates a catastrophic flooding scenario, integrating Active Directory domains, industrial controllers, virtualized networks, and intentionally placed vulnerabilities.

Executing Red Team Adversary Emulation

Red team operators established command-and-control infrastructure and executed a multi-stage attack kill chain across the environment, directly impacting simulated hydroelectric turbines.

Blue Team DFIR Analysis and Training

Defenders from the power utility analyzed forensic artifacts left during the exercise, inspecting network PCAPs, memory dumps, and Windows event logs to validate detection capabilities.

talks.title: Top War Stories from a TryHard Bug Bounty Hunter
talks.teaser: Recounts high-severity bug bounty discoveries from live hacking events, detailing complex chains from SQL injection to remote code execution.
talks.summary:
Inside Live Hacking Events

Live hacking competitions bring together elite security researchers to find critical vulnerabilities in enterprise assets under tight time constraints.

Chaining Bugs from Simple to Complex

Detailed breakdowns of high-severity submissions illustrate how seemingly minor flaws can be chained into devastating exploits, including mass PII leakage and surveillance device hijacking.

High Bounty Exploitation Case Studies

Technical walk-throughs explain critical findings—earning $10,000 to $60,000 bounties each—that leveraged SQL injections, authentication bypasses, and remote code execution.

Lessons Learned and Hunter Mindset

Succeeding in competitive bug bounties requires perseverance through failures, systematic target enumeration, and deep exploration of unexpected application behavior.

talks.title: Bridging Space and Medicine
talks.teaser: Explores the application of holographic communications in space missions and its potential to revolutionize remote medical procedures.
talks.summary:
Holographic Communications in Space

Holographic teleportation combines 3D capture and low-latency data transmission to enable lifelike interactive communication between astronauts and ground mission controllers.

Applications in Remote Medicine

Applying holographic communication technologies to terrestrial and remote healthcare enables specialist surgical consultations and medical training across extreme geographic distances.

Technological and Network Horizons

Advancing real-time spatial computing platforms transforms how medical expertise is projected to isolated operational environments on Earth and in orbit.

talks.title: Tough Adversary: Don’t Blame Sun Tzu
talks.teaser: Analyzes military academy curricula and operational philosophy from China and Russia to explain the strategic foundations of foreign cyber adversaries.
talks.summary:
Operational Frustrations in Cyber Defense

Despite advanced technical capabilities and trained operators, national security cyber operations often struggle with persistent adversary resilience in contested cyberspace.

The Role of Adversarial Philosophy

Understanding adversary campaigns requires analyzing underlying strategic philosophy rather than focusing exclusively on tactical tools and techniques.

Insights from Foreign Military Academies

Examining contemporary curricula and published literature from Russian and Chinese military academies reveals how foreign strategists conceptualize information warfare and multi-domain operations.

Reorienting Defensive Strategy

Western cyber defense paradigms must incorporate philosophical and holistic perspectives to anticipate adversary moves and protect critical national infrastructure.

talks.title: The Risk and Reward of Distributed Industrial Control
talks.teaser: Examines how remote monitoring in distributed energy resources expands industrial attack surfaces, drawing lessons from the 2022 ViaSat attack.
talks.summary:
Distributed Operations in Industrial Assets

Economic efficiencies and automation have led operators of distributed energy resources (DERs), pipelines, and wind farms to rely heavily on unmanned remote control over public and satellite networks.

Expanding the Attack Surface

Transitioning from isolated facilities to distributed network architectures exposes critical physical assets to remote cyber exploitation and disruption.

Case Studies in Communication Link Interruption

Analyzing historical adversary campaigns, including the 2022 ViaSat satellite communications compromise and pipeline intrusions, highlights how fragile communication channels can be exploited.

Sensible Risk Mitigation Strategies

Securing distributed industrial operations requires cost-effective architectural hardening, robust encryption, and out-of-band monitoring without requiring cost-prohibitive dedicated fiber networks.

talks.title: Color Blasted Badge Making: How Hard Could It Be?
talks.teaser: Hardware creators compare different engineering approaches, tradeoffs, and design lessons learned when building multicolor electronic badges.
talks.summary:
Engineering Multicolor Electronic Badges

Developing custom conference badges featuring vibrant, multicolor displays and LED matrices presents distinct hardware, software, and power management hurdles.

Comparing Maker Approaches

Three independent badge makers share their divergent engineering architectures, evaluating the strengths and weaknesses of different PCB fabrication and display techniques.

Manufacturing Realities and Pitfalls

Navigating component procurement, surface-mount assembly, and firmware flashing under strict event timelines highlights crucial lessons for embedded creators.

Advice for Community Hardware Builders

Practical recommendations help aspiring hardware creators avoid common design mistakes when embarking on complex electronic badge projects.

talks.title: Famous and Not So Famous Unsolved Codes
talks.teaser: Examines legendary unsolved ciphers and encrypted artifacts including Kryptos, the Voynich manuscript, and historical wartime messages.
talks.summary:
The Enduring Allure of Unsolved Ciphers

Throughout history, mysterious encrypted texts and physical artifacts have resisted cryptanalysis, intriguing mathematicians, historians, and cybersecurity researchers.

Legendary Sculptures and Ciphers

Researchers analyze famous unsolved puzzles, including the Kryptos sculpture at CIA Headquarters, the Australian NKrypt installation, and the enigmatic Voynich manuscript.

Historical and Wartime Puzzles

Case studies examine encrypted engravings on 20th-century artifacts, WWII carrier pigeon messages recovered from chimneys, and cipher letters penned by historical criminal defendants.

Modern Cryptanalytic Methods

Applying contemporary statistical techniques and computational analysis offers new avenues for decoding historical encrypted records.

talks.title: An Adversarial Approach to Airline Revenue Management Proving Ground
talks.teaser: Dissects airline fare calculation and revenue management systems from an adversarial mindset to uncover architectural constraints and flaws.
talks.summary:
Economics of Airline Revenue Management

Airlines operate under extreme capital costs, landing slot limits, and bilateral treaties, utilizing sophisticated dynamic pricing engines to maximize flight yields.

Demystifying Fares and Ticketing Architecture

A technical overview of Global Distribution Systems (GDS), published tariff categories, and booking code structures clarifies how airline tickets are generated.

Identifying System Constraints and Weaknesses

Applying an adversarial hacker perspective reveals how legacy protocol constraints, booking class logic bugs, and fare rule edge cases introduce systemic vulnerabilities.

Researching Travel Technology Security

Understanding underlying ticketing infrastructure equips researchers to investigate pricing engines and API endpoints across specialized travel platforms.

talks.title: Navigating the Turbulent Skies of Aviation Cyber Regulation
talks.teaser: Examines technical and policy challenges in civil aviation security as new European and United States regulatory frameworks take effect.
talks.summary:
The Changing Aviation Regulatory Landscape

With expanding connectivity across aircraft and ground support networks, aviation authorities in the United States and Europe are rolling out comprehensive cybersecurity mandates.

Bridging Policy Intent with Technical Reality

Regulators, airlines, and aerospace manufacturers face challenges in reconciling rigid compliance frameworks with complex airborne software architectures.

Operational Hurdles in Civil Aviation

Implementing continuous vulnerability disclosure, supply chain validation, and incident response requirements across global airline fleets requires substantial coordination.

Strategies for Effective Compliance

Industry stakeholders discuss practical strategies for aligning technical security controls with international regulatory compliance to protect global airspace.

talks.title: Exposing Attacks Hiding in the Sheer Noise of False Positives
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how open-source data science models cluster heterogeneous security alerts to uncover coordinated multi-stage cyber attacks.
talks.summary:
The Alert Fatigue Challenge in SOCs

Modern security operations centers (SOCs) are overwhelmed by millions of daily security logs, alerts, and false positives, obscuring subtle indicators of sophisticated intrusions.

Clustering Heterogeneous Security Data

Leveraging open-source data science models and machine learning pipelines enables automated grouping of disparate log events based on behavioral similarities.

Reconstructing Attack Kill Chains

Encoding security domain knowledge into clustering algorithms transforms noisy telemetry into correlated multi-stage attack narratives and actionable intelligence.

Enhancing Security Operations Efficiency

Deploying automated alert clustering significantly reduces analyst fatigue and accelerates incident triage without requiring dedicated data science expertise.

talks.title: Data on Demand: The Challenges of Building a Privacy Focused AI Device
talks.teaser: Details architectural and data pipeline practices used at Rabbit to secure customer identities, anonymize voice data, and control RAG model access.
talks.summary:
Privacy Dilemmas in Consumer AI Devices

Building standalone AI hardware products requires collecting extensive user identity, audio, and personal context data, necessitating strong privacy-by-design architectures.

Identity Management and Credential Isolation

Designing authentication pipelines to collect and manage customer web credentials securely prevents lateral unauthorized data access.

Voice Telemetry Anonymization Pipelines

Processing, logging, and anonymizing customer voice interactions in real time prevents sensitive voice biometric leaks during model training.

Just In Time Context Access for RAG Models

Implementing strict 'just-in-time' access policies ensures retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) models only ingest contextual data when explicitly authorized by users.

talks.title: D0N0H4RM: Cyber STEM Storytime
talks.teaser: Panelists share stories and strategies for advancing cybersecurity education, youth mentorship, and STEM outreach initiatives.

talks.title: Hacker vs. AI: Perspectives from an Ex-Spy
talks.teaser: An ex-intelligence specialist uses pop culture narratives and live demos to demystify AI threats in real-world national security operations.
talks.summary:
Myths and Realities of AI in Intelligence

The intersection of artificial intelligence and national security is frequently distorted by science fiction tropes and media hype. Real-world applications require distinguishing tangible capabilities from fiction.

Pop Culture Lenses on Cyber Warfare

Utilizing narrative concepts from Ghost in the Shell and Neuromancer provides an accessible framework to examine state surveillance, algorithmic targeting, and autonomous cyber operations.

Under the Hood Machine Learning Demos

Live demonstrations illustrate how machine learning algorithms operate within intelligence analysis, highlighting their functional strengths alongside critical adversarial blind spots.

Human Agency in Countering AI Threats

Preserving human oversight and ethical boundaries is vital to preventing uncontrolled autonomous surveillance and securing national cyber systems.

talks.title: Responding to Breaches, Ransomware, and State-Sponsored Threat Actors
talks.teaser: Security leaders analyze recent high-profile breaches, state-sponsored TTPs, and effective containment strategies for enterprise defenders.
talks.summary:
Surge in Targeted Cyber Threats

Organizations face unprecedented waves of targeted ransomware operations and state-sponsored espionage targeting critical infrastructure, corporate assets, and democratic institutions.

Why Well-Equipped Defenses Still Fail

Panelists examine why enterprises with substantial security budgets and modern defensive tools continue to suffer breaches, identifying visibility gaps and configuration drift.

Effective Containment and Incident Response

Rapid containment strategies, clear escalation protocols, and rehearsed incident management playbooks are critical to mitigating business damage during active compromises.

Leveraging Threat Intel and Attack Simulation

Incorporating proactive cyber threat intelligence and realistic adversary emulation helps defenders understand attacker mindsets and validate detection posture.

talks.title: DIY Pharmaceuticals
talks.teaser: Demonstrates open-source automated chemical synthesis pathways and MicroLab hardware for low-cost decentralized medicine production.
talks.summary:
The Crisis of Medication Access

High pharmaceutical pricing and intellectual property monopolies prevent millions of patients worldwide from accessing lifesaving cures, such as direct-acting antivirals for Hepatitis C.

Decentralized Drug Synthesis Pathways

Researchers developed open-source chemical synthesis workflows that reduce the production cost of essential curative therapies from tens of thousands of dollars to accessible price points.

The MicroLab Automated Chemical Reactor

Utilizing digital research assistants, automated chemical coding, and the open-source MicroLab automated reaction chamber allows users to synthesize and tablet essential medicines.

Legal and Ethical Dimensions of Open Science

The intersection of intellectual property law, biohacking, and humanitarian access challenges traditional definitions of pharmaceutical regulation.

talks.summary:
DEF CON Conference Presentation

This segment features remarks and presentations from DEF CON organizers and security leaders. Topics include the state of cybersecurity, hacker culture, community initiatives, and the conference's impact on the security landscape.

talks.title: Got 99 Problems but Prompt Injection Ain't Pineapple
talks.teaser: Explores the ethical challenges of AI vulnerability disclosure, covering data bias exploitation and responsible reporting standards.
talks.summary:
Vulnerability Disclosure in Artificial Intelligence

Disclosing vulnerabilities in AI models presents unique hurdles compared to traditional software, requiring a balance between public transparency and preventing widespread exploitation.

Data Bias and Model Manipulation Vectors

Adversaries exploit algorithmic biases, data poisoning, and model manipulation techniques that can amplify vulnerability impact across automated decision-making systems.

Case Studies in Recent AI Disclosures

Evaluating real-world AI vulnerability disclosures highlights inconsistencies in vendor responses, patch validation, and public reporting mechanisms.

Refining Responsible AI Disclosure Frameworks

Establishing unified industry standards for AI vulnerability reporting fosters public trust and ensures consistent remediation across machine learning deployments.

talks.title: Custom, Cheap, Easy, and Safe Badges Without Starting from Scratch
talks.teaser: Presents OpenTaxus, an open-source hardware badge platform customizable via KiCad and CircuitPython for low-cost mass production.
talks.summary:
The High Costs of Custom Event Badges

Designing electronic conference badges from scratch involves immense investments of time, funding, PCB prototyping, component sourcing, and assembly logistics.

Introducing the OpenTaxus Badge Platform

OpenTaxus provides an open-source, affordable, and readily mass-producible badge reference architecture that event organizers can quickly customize.

Customizing Hardware and Software

Walkthroughs demonstrate modifying circuit board schematics and artwork in KiCad and writing interactive application features using CircuitPython.

Budgeting, Logistics, and Manufacturing Pitfalls

Practical guidance covers minimizing Bill of Materials (BOM) costs, managing component lead times, and avoiding common hardware failure modes during event deployments.

talks.teaser: Recounts intriguing bug bounty stories ranging from simple logic errors to chaining CAPTCHA weaknesses to break sensitive application encryption.
talks.summary:
The Spectrum of Bug Bounty Discoveries

Bug bounty hunting involves finding vulnerabilities that range from surprisingly straightforward logic flaws to intricate multi-stage exploit chains.

Capitalizing on Simple Vulnerabilities

Real-world examples illustrate how simple observation during routine browsing revealed business logic flaws that allowed infinite balance manipulation.
