Hacker Intuition and Persistence

Developing strong investigative intuition and persisting through ambiguous application behaviors are vital skills for discovering high-impact security bugs.

talks.title: Exploiting Bluetooth from Your Car to the Bank Account
talks.teaser: Releases BlueToolkit and discloses 64 Bluetooth Classic vulnerabilities across 22 modern cars and aircraft flight management systems.
talks.summary:
Infotainment Attack Surface Expansion

Modern automotive infotainment and aviation flight management systems increasingly integrate Bluetooth Classic stacks, often operating with unpatched firmware due to complex update logistics.

Introducing the BlueToolkit Framework

Researchers developed BlueToolkit, an open-source testing framework designed to systematically test, fuzz, and replay Bluetooth Classic protocol vulnerabilities.

Disclosing 64 Zero Day Vulnerabilities

Applying BlueToolkit uncovered sixty-four new vulnerabilities across twenty-two vehicle models and the Garmin Flight Stream aviation management system.

Man in the Middle and Account Hijacking

Demonstrated exploits show how implementation flaws enable attackers to establish man-in-the-middle positions, exfiltrate sensitive data, and escalate privileges to hijack user accounts.

talks.title: Hunters and Gatherers: A Deep Dive into the World of Bug Bounties
talks.teaser: Bug bounty program managers and researchers discuss submission quality, triage dynamics, and strategies for maturing bug bounty programs.
talks.summary:
Dynamics of the Bug Bounty Ecosystem

A panel of experienced program managers and security researchers examines the evolving relationship between bug bounty hunters and corporate security teams.

Enhancing Submission Impact and Quality

Hunters share strategies for providing clear reproduction steps and business impact analysis, ensuring reports are quickly prioritized by triage analysts.

Managing and Maturing Bounty Programs

Program managers provide actionable recommendations for organizations looking to scale bug bounty programs while managing report volume and internal engineering bandwidth.

Future Trends in Vulnerability Crowdsourcing

Panelists explore the impact of emerging technologies and automated AI tooling on the future trajectory of crowdsourced security testing.

talks.title: Eradicating Hepatitis C with BioTerrorism
talks.teaser: Presents an automated chemical synthesis pathway on open hardware to produce low-cost antiviral treatments and bypass drug monopolies.
talks.summary:
Addressing Preventable Viral Deaths

Hepatitis C causes hundreds of thousands of preventable deaths annually despite the existence of highly effective curative antiviral medications like Sofosbuvir.

Overcoming Patent and Monopoly Barriers

Exorbitant drug pricing by patent holders restricts access to life-saving medications, motivating open-source alternatives for chemical synthesis.

Automated Chemical Synthesis on Open Hardware

Demonstrating the MicroLab open-source automated reactor shows how digital literature assistants generate executable synthesis code to produce pharmaceutical tablets for a fraction of commercial costs.

Ethics of Decentralized Medical Manufacturing

The intersection of intellectual property laws and humanitarian medicine highlights the growing right-to-health movement within biohacking communities.

talks.title: Human Dignity in AI and Tech Policy
talks.teaser: Examines how data-driven behavioral profiling undermines human agency and proposes policy frameworks centered on human dignity in tech regulation.
talks.summary:
Online Manipulation and Generative AI

Decades of social media profiling have established data-driven architectures capable of manipulating human decision-making and consumer behavior.

Information Asymmetries and Loss of Agency

Market dynamics and targeted behavioral design create deep information asymmetries, turning individuals into predictable, programmable subjects.

Centering Human Dignity in Tech Law

Legal and regulatory frameworks must establish human dignity as a non-negotiable principle, protecting fundamental rights to privacy, autonomy, and non-discrimination.

Beyond Compliance to Structural Protections

Reclaiming personal dignity requires moving beyond simple consent banners to enforce substantive limits on automated behavioral profiling and AI manipulation.

talks.title: Leveraging AI for Smarter Bug Bounties
talks.teaser: Details the development of an autonomous generative AI agent designed to augment offensive bug bounty and penetration testing workflows.
talks.summary:
AI in Offensive Security Research

While defensive AI applications have expanded rapidly, the role of autonomous generative AI agents in offensive security and vulnerability research is still emerging.

Designing an Offensive AI Agent

Researchers built a practical AI agent capable of mimicking human intuition, automating reconnaissance, and identifying subtle application vulnerabilities.

Augmenting Bug Bounty Workflows

Integrating the AI assistant into bug bounty testing accelerates endpoint discovery, payload formulation, and vulnerability hypothesis testing.

Implications for the Future of Penetration Testing

Evaluating the performance of autonomous AI agents highlights how machine learning will transform offensive tradecraft and bug bounty competition.

talks.title: ICS 101
talks.teaser: Introduces industrial control systems architecture, the Purdue model, attacker viewpoints, and steps to build a personal ICS research lab.
talks.summary:
Introduction to Industrial Control Systems

Industrial Control Systems (ICS) and Operational Technology (OT) govern physical processes across manufacturing, power generation, and water treatment utilities.

The Purdue Enterprise Reference Architecture

Understanding the Purdue model provides the structural framework for how field controllers, human-machine interfaces (HMIs), and enterprise IT networks communicate.

The Attacker View of Industrial Architecture

Examining industrial networks from an adversary perspective highlights common exposure points, protocol trust assumptions, and engineering workstation vulnerabilities.

Building a Home ICS Research Lab

Practical guidance details equipment selection, PLC simulators, and communication software to help researchers build their own physical or virtual ICS testing environments.

talks.title: GPS Spoofing: It's About Time, Not Just Position
talks.teaser: Analyzes how GPS coarse time spoofing invalidates digital certificates on aircraft, grounding fleets and disrupting avionics communications.
talks.summary:
The Overlooked Vector of GPS Time Spoofing

Media coverage of GPS spoofing and jamming predominantly focuses on geographic position errors, neglecting the severe impact of manipulation on precision time synchronization.

Real World Incident of Future Time Spoofing

A documented aviation incident revealed how spoofing GPS time forward into the future invalidated onboard digital certificates and paralyzed electronic communications.

Grounding Aircraft and System Recovery

Because avionics GPS clocks incorporate protections against backward time shifts but lack forward roll guards, aircraft required weeks of maintenance to reflash systems and reset clocks.

Mitigations for Aerospace Navigation Systems

Developing resilient timing safeguards and validating conventional radio navigation aids are essential to protect global aviation fleets against spoofing attacks.

talks.title: MFT: Malicious Fungible Tokens
talks.teaser: Introduces mFT, an open-source tool demonstrating how to use blockchain-backed non-fungible tokens as immutable command-and-control infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Blockchain Backed Command and Control

Command and control (C2) infrastructure is routinely disrupted by domain seizures, IP blocklists, and hosting takedowns. Utilizing public blockchain smart contracts provides adversaries with decentralized, takedown-resistant channels.

Relaying Commands via Non Fungible Tokens

Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) deployed on public ledgers can store and relay encoded payload directives, system fingerprinting queries, and data exfiltration markers.

The mFT Automated Payload Tool

Researchers built 'mFT', an open-source toolkit that automates generating malicious NFT payloads and provides safe sample tokens for defensive testing.

Defensive Detection and Ledger Analysis

Monitoring public blockchain transactions and smart contract state changes enables defenders to identify covert C2 relay activities across enterprise networks.

talks.title: Master Splinter’s Initial Physical Access Dojo
talks.teaser: Presents a comic-style narrative of a complex red team engagement achieving physical datacenter access entirely through social engineering.
talks.summary:
Narrative Breakdown of Physical Red Teaming

Executing complex physical intrusions without relying on lockpicking or exploit kits requires structured social engineering tradecraft and precise operational execution.

Pretexting, Reconnaissance, and Role Allocation

From initial client scoping to on-site surveillance, specialized social engineering teams coordinate personas, deceptive pretexts, and intelligence gathering.

Infiltrating Corporate Datacenters

Case studies demonstrate gaining physical entry into high-security corporate facilities and server rooms within three weeks by leveraging psychological manipulation and trust heuristics.

Methodological Lessons for Human Layer Defense

Building resilience against social engineering demands continuous staff training, strict visitor verification protocols, and reducing single points of human failure.

talks.title: GUR RIBYHGVBA BS PELCGBTENCUL
talks.teaser: Traces the historical evolution and etymology of cryptographic concepts, exploring terminology misuse and data secrecy tradeoffs.
talks.summary:
Etymology and Classical Cryptographic Concepts

Modern digital terminology frequently conflates encoding, enciphering, and encryption. Investigating classical definitions clarifies the foundational principles of cryptographic science.

Evolution of Terminology in the Digital Era

Analyzing historical usage from classical ciphers to modern algorithms highlights how shifted meanings impact our conceptual understanding of data security.

Secrecy versus Identity Privacy Tradeoffs

Evaluating the tension between keeping data confidential and preserving user anonymity illustrates core dilemmas in contemporary cryptographic implementation.

Preserving Foundational Security Objectives

Revisiting classical security principles helps modern practitioners maintain rigorous security design standards and accurate technical communication.

talks.title: Fitness of Physical Red Teamers
talks.teaser: Shares physical conditioning strategies, movement training routines, and field war stories to optimize endurance for physical red team operations.
talks.summary:
Physical Demands of On-Site Assessments

While digital red teaming emphasizes technical tooling, physical penetration tests demand sustained mobility, agility, climbing capability, and situational endurance.

Targeted Conditioning for Red Team Operators

Developing peak physical conditioning requires structured training routines tailored to stealthy movement, obstacle scaling, and sustained physical exertion.

Field War Stories and Performance Comparisons

Operators share lessons learned from real-world facility assessments, comparing physical performance metrics and mission outcomes before and after structured fitness regimens.

Accessible Hotel Room Training Routines

Practical bodyweight exercises and conditioning habits allow security practitioners to maintain peak physical readiness while traveling for on-site engagements.

talks.title: I Am Still the Captain Now!
talks.teaser: Examines maritime vessel cybersecurity, analyzes the MV Dali incident, and reviews emerging IACS UR E26 and E27 cyber regulations.
talks.summary:
Maritime Vessel Security Posture

Modern commercial maritime vessels integrate complex operational technology, satellite communications, and automated navigation systems that present substantial cyber risks.

Technical Analysis of the MV Dali Incident

Examining the technical realities behind the MV Dali bridge collision dispels widespread misinformation while illustrating how maritime systems remain vulnerable to cyber events.

Emerging Maritime Cyber Regulations

International Association of Classification Societies (IACS) Unified Requirements E26 and E27 introduce mandatory cybersecurity baselines for onboard equipment and vessel integration.

Preparing Fleet Operators for Compliance

Ship operators and technology providers must implement continuous monitoring, asset inventories, and secure configuration management across maritime fleets.

talks.title: Evading Modern Defenses When Phishing with Pixels
talks.teaser: Explores QR code phishing tactics, visual obfuscation methods, and Outlook email rendering quirks used to evade modern email defenses.
talks.summary:
Mechanics of QR Code Phishing

QR code phishing (quishing) embeds deceptive links within images to bypass traditional email gateway URL scanners and trick users into scanning codes with mobile devices.

Visual Obfuscation and Pixel Manipulation

Applying visual fragmentation, color palette shifts, and layered pixel manipulation techniques ensures QR codes remain decodable by phone cameras while blinding automated computer vision filters.

Exploiting Outlook Rendering Engine Quirks

Analyzing the HTML parsing and rendering behavior of the Microsoft Outlook desktop client reveals formatting techniques that disguise image payloads from security filters.

Hardening Email Defenses Against Quishing

Defenders must upgrade gateway inspection pipelines to render dynamic email HTML, extract embedded QR images, and enforce multi-factor authentication across mobile devices.

talks.title: Locksport Competitions: Compete in the Olympics of Locks
talks.teaser: Explores competitive locksport events around the world, detailing tournament formats, preparation strategies, and techniques to win.
talks.summary:
In this comprehensive presentation on the DEF CON 32 Creator Stage, a competitive locksport enthusiast delivers a detailed guide to competitive lockpicking tournaments around the world, dubbed the "Olympics of Locks." At 04:00, the speaker highlights major international gatherings, focusing on the Dutch Open organized by Toool in the Netherlands, where the world's most skilled lockpickers compete in timed head-to-head heats.

The talk outlines standard competition formats at 08:00, detailing how contestants race against the clock to manipulate unknown, high-security mechanical cylinders. At 12:00, the speaker demonstrates safe manipulation techniques, showing how paper gradient stickers attached to safe dials enable lockpickers to detect microscopic contact point variations.

At 16:00, the session covers specialized locksport categories, including lever lock impressioning, wafer picking, and non-destructive automotive entry. The presenter concludes at 20:00 by exploring master keying contests and accessible lockpicking competitions designed for visually impaired participants, welcoming newcomers to join local locksport clubs and develop their mechanical puzzle-solving abilities. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Manufacturing Lessons Learned, Lessons Taught
talks.teaser: Analyzes why manufacturing remains the primary target for ransomware operators and how IIoT connectivity trends impact OT network defense.
talks.summary:
Ransomware Targeting in Manufacturing

Annual threat intelligence reports consistently identify manufacturing as the most targeted industrial vertical for ransomware attacks, accounting for up to seventy percent of victim organizations.

Factors Driving High Victimization Rates

Flat network architectures, legacy unsegmented OT environments, low operational margins, and absence of standardized compliance regimes leave manufacturers uniquely vulnerable.

Hyper Connected IIoT and Cloud Risks

While hyper-connected Industrial IoT devices enable advanced production efficiencies and predictive maintenance, they bridge external cloud environments directly into OT control networks.

Roadmap for Securing Industrial Networks

Lessons learned from manufacturing operational disruptions provide a practical blueprint for hardening network perimeters, segmenting critical processes, and securing IIoT connections.

talks.title: Introduction to IPv6
talks.teaser: Demystifies IPv6 networking principles, comparing modern address architecture against legacy IPv4 design limitations.
talks.summary:
The Reality of IPv4 Depletion

While the modern Internet continues to operate largely on IPv4, address exhaustion and Network Address Translation (NAT) have distorted the original end-to-end vision of internet connectivity.

IPv6 Architectural Fundamentals

Understanding IPv6 requires exploring its expanded 128-bit address space, stateless address autoconfiguration (SLAAC), and simplified header structures.

Security Implications for Practitioners

Despite widespread network deployment, many cybersecurity practitioners lack familiarity with IPv6 routing behaviors, neighbor discovery vulnerabilities, and dual-stack exposure risks.

Unlocking Full IPv6 Capabilities

Mastering IPv6 addressing models, subnetting conventions, and packet structures enables engineers to design secure, next-generation network architectures.

talks.title: MoWireless MoProblems: Modular Wireless Survey System & Data Analytics
talks.teaser: Details the design of a modular wireless survey platform and PacketGlass, an Elasticsearch visualization pipeline processing raw 802.11 PCAP data.
talks.summary:
Large Scale Wireless Reconnaissance Challenges

Collecting massive volumes of wireless network data across extensive geographical areas produces terabytes of raw packet captures that are difficult to index and analyze efficiently.

Modular Hardware Survey Platform

Researchers built a modular survey rig capable of capturing multi-band 802.11 Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and SDR signals concurrently, integrating Kismet data streams and raw PCAPs.

PacketGlass Analytical Visualization Engine

To manage captured telemetry, the team created PacketGlass, an Elasticsearch and Kibana analytical platform that parses, ingests, and visualizes tens of millions of wireless devices.

Operationalizing Wireless Telemetry

Advanced querying pipelines enable researchers to track device movements, identify rogue access points, and analyze wireless threat vectors at scale.

talks.title: Dysfunctional Unity: The Road to Nowhere
talks.teaser: Discusses systemic vulnerabilities in hospital medical device topologies and examines common misconceptions regarding Software Bills of Materials.
talks.summary:
Persistent Vulnerabilities in Medical Topologies

Hospital networks continue to house legacy, unpatched medical devices, creating high-risk environments that attract regulatory scrutiny from CISA and the FDA.

Misconceptions Surrounding Medical SBOMs

Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) are often viewed as complete security solutions. However, inaccurate inventory parsing and lack of automated dependency tracking limit their standalone effectiveness.

Analyzing Medical Device CVE Trends

Examining disclosed CVEs across clinical equipment highlights recurring architectural flaws in embedded operating systems, default network services, and unauthenticated management ports.

A Pragmatic Security Roadmap for Healthcare

Building resilient hospital environments requires implementing strict network micro-segmentation, continuous asset discovery, and coordinated vulnerability disclosure with device manufacturers.

talks.title: Exploiting Voice Cloning in Adversarial Simulation
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how deep learning voice cloning bypasses enterprise voice verification systems in realistic adversarial simulations.
talks.summary:
Rise of Voice Verification Systems

Financial institutions and customer service help desks increasingly rely on voice biometric authentication to verify caller identities during sensitive account operations.

Deep Learning Voice Cloning Capabilities

Advancements in neural acoustic modeling allow researchers to generate highly convincing synthetic voice clones from only brief public audio samples.

Bypassing Enterprise Voice Biometrics

Recorded adversary simulations demonstrate how cloned voice samples successfully bypass automated voice verification systems across several major commercial institutions.

Defensive Countermeasures for Red and Blue Teams

Red teams require structured frameworks to emulate synthetic voice attacks, while defensive teams must implement multi-factor verification checks to mitigate AI-driven pretexting.

talks.title: MicroHard More Like MicroEasy to Exploit
talks.teaser: Details command injection and buffer overflow vulnerabilities in Microhard long-range industrial radio hardware used across SCADA networks.
talks.summary:
Microhard Equipment in Critical Infrastructure

Microhard manufactures industrial long-range wireless modems and routers widely deployed across SCADA networks, power utilities, and point-of-sale systems.

Firmware Analysis and Vulnerability Discovery

Security analysis of Microhard radio firmware revealed numerous critical vulnerabilities, including unauthenticated OS command injections and memory corruption buffer overflows.

Vague Vendor Release Notes and Patching Gaps

Reviewing manufacturer security advisories exposes how critical vulnerability fixes were obscured within vague release notes, leaving asset owners unaware of severe exposure.

Lessons in Secure Hardware Development

Remediating industrial radio vulnerabilities requires vendors to implement robust secure development lifecycles, static analysis checks, and transparent vulnerability reporting.

talks.title: Incubated ML Exploits: Backdooring ML Pipelines with Input Handling Bugs
talks.teaser: Demonstrates incubated ML exploits using LangSec principles to inject backdoors into machine learning pipelines via model serialization bugs.
talks.summary:
The ML Pipeline Attack Surface

Machine learning models are not isolated files; they are complex artifacts generated and processed by extensive toolchains, serialization libraries, and automated pipelines.

Language Theoretic Security (LangSec) in ML

Applying LangSec principles reveals that model parsers frequently contain input-handling and deserialization vulnerabilities that can be exploited during model ingestion.

Constructing Polyglot and Ambiguous Artifacts

Researchers crafted malicious polyglot and ambiguous model files that evade static scanners while executing arbitrary backdoor triggers when loaded by ML frameworks.

Advancing Fickling and ML Security Guidelines

Contributions to Fickling, a pickle security tool for ML, along with practical development guidelines, help practitioners secure model serialization workflows.

talks.title: National Labs Use of XR
talks.teaser: Examines how Pacific Northwest National Laboratory utilizes extended reality platforms for 3D digital twins, hazardous training, and threat simulations.
talks.summary:
Extended Reality in Federal Research

Department of Energy National Laboratories explore disruptive technologies to advance national security, critical infrastructure protection, and emergency operations.

Building Immersive 3D Digital Twins

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) creates high-fidelity 3D virtual twins of specialized laboratory facilities, enabling remote scientists to interact with unique research equipment.

Simulating Hazardous Environments

Immersive XR platforms simulate hazardous material spills and dangerous operational scenarios that cannot be safely reproduced in physical training facilities.

Public Outreach and Security Threat Visualization

Leveraging interactive XR simulations enhances stakeholder communication, visualizing complex cybersecurity threats to critical infrastructure for public and government sponsors.

talks.title: Decoding Galah: An LLM-Powered Web Honeypot
talks.teaser: Presents Galah, an LLM-powered web honeypot that dynamically generates authentic HTTP responses to emulate diverse web applications.
talks.summary:
Limitations of Low Interaction Web Honeypots

Traditional low-interaction honeypots rely on static templates to emulate web services, allowing automated scanners and attackers to detect honeypot signatures quickly.

Introducing the Galah LLM Honeypot

Galah utilizes large language models to generate dynamic, context-aware HTTP response headers and bodies in response to incoming attacker requests from a single prompt.

Benchmarking LLMs for HTTP Response Generation

Evaluating multiple language models determines their speed, fidelity, and reliability in generating authentic server responses that mimic diverse web applications.

Attacker Engagement Dynamics

Deploying Galah on the public Internet reveals how realistic, LLM-generated HTTP responses significantly increase attacker dwell time and capture novel payload interactions.

talks.title: Ground Control to Major Threat: Hacking the Space Link Extension Protocol
talks.teaser: Analyzes security vulnerabilities in the Space Link Extension protocol used by NASA and ESA, demonstrating ground station traffic interception.
talks.summary:
Targeting Space Ground Segment Infrastructure

While satellite security discussions frequently emphasize direct RF jamming, attacking terrestrial ground segment infrastructure is often far more accessible and potent for adversaries.

The Space Link Extension (SLE) Standard

The SLE protocol standardizes communication between space mission data centers and distributed tracking ground stations across major space agencies, including NASA and ESA.

Protocol Vulnerabilities and Hijacking Vectors

Architectural weaknesses in SLE implementations enable malicious actors to conduct denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, intercept unencrypted telemetry, and inject unauthorized spacecraft commands.

Protocol Level Mitigation Strategies

Hardening space communications requires integrating mandatory mutual authentication, cryptographic signing, and robust transport encryption into the core SLE protocol standard.

talks.title: Kubernetes Attack Simulation: The Definitive Guide
talks.teaser: Provides a practical blueprint for Kubernetes purple team threat emulation, container security monitoring, and detection engineering.
talks.summary:
Transitioning SOCs to Containerized Environments

Migrating enterprise workloads to Kubernetes transforms SOC responsibilities from monitoring conventional host systems to building detective controls for container orchestrators.

Threat Emulation in Modern Cloud Infrastructure

Offensive security practitioners must adapt adversary emulation frameworks to model container escapes, RBAC privilege escalation, and lateral movement in Kubernetes clusters.

Purple Teaming for Container Defense

Collaborative purple team exercises allow red and blue teams to execute attack scenarios, evaluate audit log telemetry, and tune detection alerts collaboratively.

Actionable Advice for Detection Engineering

Structured guidance outlines essential Kubernetes telemetry sources, high-fidelity alerting rules, and strategies for validating container runtime defenses.

talks.title: How I Hacked Learning Codes of the Key Fob of a Car Assembled in My Country
talks.teaser: Demonstrates hardware analysis of an automotive key fob using a logic analyzer and HackRF to clone unprotected learning code RF signals.
talks.summary:
Automotive Keyless Entry Security

Modern vehicles typically implement cryptographic rolling code algorithms to prevent keyless entry signals from being captured and replayed by unauthorized attackers.

Hardware Disassembly and Chip Identification

Disassembling a key fob from a locally assembled vehicle revealed an HS2240 integrated circuit configured to transmit vulnerable learning codes rather than secure rolling codes.

Signal Capture with Logic Analyzers and SDRs

Analyzing circuit emissions with a logic analyzer confirmed predictable RF transmissions, which were then captured and replayed using a HackRF software-defined radio.

Replay Exploitation and Automotive Vulnerabilities

Because learning codes lack cryptographic replay protection, captured transmissions allow attackers to unlock vehicle doors repeatedly without the original key.

talks.title: Doors, Cameras, & Mantraps Oh My!
talks.teaser: Covers fundamental techniques for evaluating physical security controls including doors, cameras, and mantraps during client assessments.
talks.summary:
Security consultant "The Magician" provides an entry-level masterclass on the practical aspects of physical security assessments and client communication at the DEF CON 32 Creator Stage.

[03:38] The speaker breaks down the common physical vulnerabilities encountered during facility assessments, detailing bypasses for improperly installed commercial doors, latch slipping, under-door tools, and manipulating insecure window latches.

[07:12] The talk explores RFID badge cloning using portable devices like the Flipper Zero, discussing why card cloning is only one component of a comprehensive physical assessment. The Magician emphasizes the human and consultative side of physical penetration testing [10:38], explaining how to deliver constructive, empathetic client reports that focus on positive risk remediation rather than embarrassing security guards or facilities managers [14:07].

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Exploiting Bluetooth from Your Car to the Bank Account
talks.teaser: Demonstrates novel Bluetooth Classic exploits across modern automotive infotainment units and avionics flight management systems.
talks.summary:
Expanding Bluetooth Attack Surfaces

Over the past decade, vehicle infotainment systems and aviation flight controllers have integrated extensive Bluetooth wireless capabilities, creating new entry points for remote attackers.

BlueToolkit Testing and Replay Framework

Researchers introduced BlueToolkit, an open-source testing platform designed to discover, fuzz, and replay Bluetooth Classic implementation vulnerabilities.

Discovering 64 Vulnerabilities Across 22 Vehicles

Security assessments using BlueToolkit uncovered sixty-four zero-day vulnerabilities across modern automobile models and the Garmin Flight Stream avionics management system.

Privilege Escalation and Account Hijacking

Demonstrated attack vectors establish man-in-the-middle positions, exfiltrate sensitive driver data, and escalate privileges to hijack online user accounts.

talks.title: How I Developed a Low-Cost Raspberry Pi-Based Device for ADS-B Spoof Detection
talks.teaser: Details Fly Catcher, a low-cost Raspberry Pi and RTL-SDR device that uses a convolutional neural network to detect spoofed ADS-B aircraft signals.
talks.summary:
The Threat of ADS-B Aviation Spoofing

Automatic Dependent Surveillance–Broadcast (ADS-B) broadcasts unencrypted aircraft flight parameters over 1090 MHz, leaving civilian aviation vulnerable to RF signal spoofing.

The Fly Catcher Hardware Architecture

Fly Catcher is a portable detection device combining a 1090 MHz antenna, FlightAware RTL-SDR receiver, custom 3D-printed enclosure, and a Raspberry Pi.

Neural Network Spoofing Classifier

A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on authentic and simulated spoofed ADS-B datasets detects signal anomalies across aircraft velocity, altitude, and location telemetry.

In-Flight Field Testing and Validation

Deploying Fly Catcher during an hour-long research flight validated its real-time radar interface and machine learning classification of nearby aircraft signals.

talks.title: From Theory to Reality: Demonstrating the Simplicity of SPARTA Techniques
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how man-in-the-middle attacks on ground infrastructure validate SPARTA framework techniques against space systems.
talks.summary:
Transitioning Space Threats to Proof of Concepts

Space cybersecurity traditionally relies on theoretical threat models. Demonstrating practical proof-of-concept attacks validates real-world operational risks for space missions.

Man in the Middle on Ground Infrastructure

Executing a simplified man-in-the-middle attack against ground station networks demonstrates how adversaries can intercept and alter communication links to active spacecraft.

Mapping to the SPARTA Framework

Practical test results map directly onto techniques within the Space Attack Research and Tactic Analysis (SPARTA) matrix, illustrating the ease of executing theorized space TTPs.

Breaking Implicit Trust in Ground Segments

Securing space assets requires dismantling implicit trust between ground stations and spacecraft by enforcing cryptographic validation throughout the entire mission lifecycle.

talks.title: Fool Us Once, Fool Us Twice: Hacking Norwegian Banks
talks.teaser: Explains how postal mail paper forms were exploited in 2021 and 2024 to gain unauthorized access to Norwegian bank accounts.
talks.summary:
Exploiting Paper Banking Workflows

In 2021, security researchers discovered that submitting a single-page paper form via postal mail could compromise personal bank accounts at the largest financial institution in Norway.

Unauthorized Access and Full Account Takeover

The vulnerability enabled unauthorized actors to transfer funds, view ten years of transaction histories, and modify customer account details without digital authentication.

Recurring Vulnerabilities in 2024

Despite previous public disclosures, the identical paper-based authentication flaw was successfully demonstrated against another major bank three years later.

Reassessing Physical Identity Verification

Financial institutions must eliminate insecure paper fallback mechanisms and enforce strong, multi-channel identity verification across all customer onboarding channels.

talks.title: Finding 0days in Vilo Home Routers
talks.teaser: Documents finding nine zero-day vulnerabilities in Vilo consumer home routers through UART interfacing, firmware reversing, and protocol analysis.
talks.summary:
Student IoT Vulnerability Research

A student research team from Brigham Young University conducted a five-month security evaluation of consumer home mesh routers manufactured by Vilo Living.

Hardware Hacking and Firmware Acquisition

Researchers identified circuit board debug headers, connected to the UART interface, analyzed bootloader output, and captured CPU flash read operations to dump the firmware.

Cloud Enumeration and Protocol Reversing

Examining cloud interactions revealed unprotected AWS S3 buckets, MQTT communications, and proprietary TCP protocols used for mobile application management.

Zero Day Discovery and Responsible Disclosure

The investigation uncovered nine zero-day flaws, including stack buffer overflows and unauthenticated command injections, highlighting common vendor disclosure hurdles.

talks.title: Top 10 Cybersecurity Trends in Critical Infrastructure for 2024
talks.teaser: Shares data-driven findings from a global survey of 300 critical infrastructure security directors analyzing emerging operational threats.
talks.summary:
Surging Threats to Critical Sectors

Critical infrastructure operators across oil, natural gas, power, water, and manufacturing face an escalating volume of complex, targeted cyber attacks.

Global Survey of 300 Security Leaders

Annual empirical survey data collected from three hundred CISOs and security directors worldwide reveals key operational hurdles and budget allocations across critical sectors.

Top 10 Operational Cyber Trends

Data-driven analysis highlights top trends, including IT/OT convergence risks, ransomware extortion escalation, supply chain vulnerabilities, and regulatory compliance pressures.

Strengthening Global Infrastructure Resilience

Comparing trends across geographic regions and industry verticals helps organizations benchmark security maturity and prioritize defensive investments.

talks.title: Inside Dash Cam Custom Protocols and Discovered 0days
talks.teaser: Analyzes connected dash cams from global manufacturers, discovering shared OEM vulnerabilities, OS command injections, and custom protocol flaws.
talks.summary:
Connected Dash Cam Attack Surface

Modern automotive dash cams increasingly incorporate Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and cellular connectivity, creating new attack surfaces that jeopardize vehicle and passenger privacy.

Firmware Extraction and Boot Logic Analysis

Researchers evaluated dash cams from manufacturers in South Korea, the United States, Germany, and China, extracting filesystems to analyze boot logic and debug ports.

Zero Day Vulnerabilities in Custom Protocols

Analysis revealed critical zero-day vulnerabilities, including unauthenticated OS command injection, logic bypasses, and insecure communications over custom protocols.

Shared OEM Hardware and Supply Chain Flaws

Testing showed that four distinct commercial dash cam models shared an identical OEM circuit board, allowing a single exploit chain to compromise multiple vendor product lines.

talks.title: No Symbols When Reversing? No Problem, Bring Your Own!
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how to generate and distribute custom FunctionID and BSim symbol databases in Ghidra to accelerate reversing stripped Go binaries.
talks.summary:
The Challenge of Stripped Binaries

Opening stripped binaries in disassemblers often presents thousands of unnamed functions, creating severe bottlenecks for malware analysts and reverse engineers.

FunctionID and BSim Databases in Ghidra

Utilizing Ghidra's FunctionID and BSim capabilities enables analysts to create reusable function signature databases and match known library code across stripped targets.

Accelerating Analysis of Golang Binaries

Applying automated symbol matching to complex Golang malware families, such as the qBit family, significantly reduces analysis time and eliminates analytical blind spots.

Scaling Symbol Datasets Across Research Teams

Sharing portable FunctionID datasets and open-source Ghidra helper scripts allows security teams to collaborate efficiently and aggregate reverse engineering insights.

talks.title: Efficient Bug Bounty Automation Techniques
talks.teaser: Presents practical automation strategies and custom tooling to discover fresh targets in bug bounty programs without triggering rate limits.
talks.summary:
Balancing Automation and Hunting Efficiency

While automation is essential for bug bounty hunters to scale reconnaissance, unoptimized tooling often leads to IP bans, WAF rate limits, and excessive cloud hosting costs.

Overcoming Infrastructure and Target Limits

Building sustainable automation pipelines requires implementing adaptive request rate throttling, intelligent proxy rotation, and smart response caching.

Discovering Fresh Targets and Attack Surface

Custom scanning workflows allow researchers to detect newly deployed subdomains and API endpoints before competing hunters identify them.

Practical Tooling and Best Practices

Actionable guidance covers selecting lightweight scanning tools, writing efficient custom scripts, and maximizing return on investment in bug bounty infrastructure.

talks.title: Cybersecurity Schoolhouse Rock
talks.teaser: Makes the case for establishing standardized K-12 cybersecurity and data privacy curricula to protect schools and build foundational defense awareness.
talks.summary:
The Growing Cyber Threat to K-12 Education

Primary and secondary schools increasingly rely on digital learning platforms, exposing students and educational institutions to phishing, scams, ransomware, and identity theft.

Absence of Standardized Cybersecurity Curricula

Despite widespread technology adoption among young children, national educational standards lack formal curricula teaching foundational data privacy and digital security concepts.

Breaking the Cycle of Ignorance

Integrating age-appropriate lessons on password hygiene, social engineering awareness, and safe internet habits equips future generations to resist online fraud.

Protecting School Districts from Ransomware

Educational administrators must implement robust data protection policies and incident response planning to safeguard student records from ransomware cartels.

talks.title: Differential Privacy Beyond Algorithm: Challenges for Deployment
talks.teaser: Examines operational challenges in deploying differential privacy systems across real-world enterprise environments and government agencies.
talks.summary:
The Promise of Differential Privacy

Differential privacy (DP) provides mathematically rigorous worst-case bounds on the amount of individual personal data that can be leaked from aggregate computational outputs.

Real World Deployments and Enterprise Adoption

Major technology corporations and government statistical agencies have deployed differential privacy systems to facilitate large-scale, privacy-preserving data analysis.

Operational Challenges Beyond Algorithms

Deploying theoretical DP algorithms in production encounters complex challenges, including calibrating privacy loss budgets, explaining guarantees to non-technical users, and preventing system misuse.

Integrating DP into Enterprise Security Stacks

Overcoming deployment barriers requires developing intuitive privacy accounting tools and integrating differential privacy with broader access control frameworks.
